explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies in situ HT-XRD as the central method and accurately explains that temperature-resolved diffraction can reveal phase transformations and crystalline oxide formation. It also provides an appropriate initial-pattern baseline and recognizes limitations involving rapid, transient, or subsurface phenomena. However, it remains generic and does not reconstruct the AlCrCoFeNi system, its BCC/B2-to-FCC/sigma evolution, selective Al/Cr oxidation, air-versus-vacuum comparison, specific heating schedule, oxygen-pressure uncertainty, or observed oxide-scale differences. It also omits the important complementary roles of SEM-EDX cross-sections and CALPHAD calculations. The proposed falsification rule is only partly discriminating because a lack of new XRD peaks could reflect thin, amorphous, weakly diffracting, or subsurface oxides rather than failure of the method. No external evidence is cited, although the claims are conventional and appropriately qualified.
